tossups.text: Vasubandhu's explication of this doctrine as well as the Lankanavatara are the some primary sources for the systematization of this doctrine. Later non-Indian Buddhist traditions such as the Huayan School also developed this doctrine through works such as Fa-Zhang's essay "On the Golden Lion." Developed theoretically during the Yogacara school, this doctrine's analysis of sva-bhava or "own-being" is explicitly rejected by Nagarjuna. One part of this doctrine relates to the "other-dependent" or "incomplete-awakening" of the bodhisattvas and relates to the "shared-reward" or "sambhoga" form of this doctrine, which allows them to be understood as a bridge in this doctrine. The first or "nirmana" form of this doctrine refers to the historical manifestation of the Buddha. FTP, name this doctrine which holds that the Buddha-nature can be understood has having three forms or bodies.

This thinker identified personal, social, and environmental conversion factors as limits to a framework he proposed. He opined that the impartial spectator was a better alternative to the veil of ignorance in defending his teacher John Rawls's "justice as fairness" concept in The Idea of Justice. He used what people can do as the basis for the capability approach he developed in his article "Equality of What?" This thinker brought attention to female infanticide in his article "More Than 100 Million Women Are Missing." In another work, he pointed to a rise in food prices, rather than a shortage of supply, as the cause of an event which killed 3 million in his native West Bengal. For 10 points, name this author of Poverty and Famines, an Indian welfare economist.

The wife of one enemy of this person is said to be condemned to be hung by a palm vine for throwing thorns at this person's feet. This man is said to have traveled on a winged horse during a journey known as the Isra and Mi'raj, or The Night Journey. His sayings and teachings are collected in the Hadiths. This prophet received the revelation of God in a cave from the angel Gibril, and he fled during the Hijra to Medina from his hometown of Mecca. For 10 points, name this founder and prophet of Islam.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for insulin and glucagon. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this insulin-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The insulin is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in insulin and glucagon.

tossups.text: It's not cilia formation, but CEP55 is a key regulator in this process during which RhoA promotes myosin II activation. Astral stimulation and relaxation are theorized to cause part of this process, which can include the creation of a phragmoplast. An actin-myosin contractile ring is formed in animals during this process, which features the construction of a cell plate in plants. A cleavage furrow forms in some cells during this process. This process has a name meaning "cell movement" and directly follows telophase. For 10 points, name this phase of the cell cycle that follows mitosis, resulting in the formation of two separate daughter cells.

This author attacked Edmund Burke's claim that wisdom is passed down through generations of nobility in Rights of Man, and argued against miraculous revelations and the divinity of the Bible in another work. He noted that "These are the times that try men's souls," in The American Crisis, and argued for independence from Britain in a 1776 pamphlet. For 10 points, name this author of The Age of Reason and Common Sense.

This author performed many of his plays at the Globe Theatre in London. He created characters like Banquo, whose ghost scares the main character in Macbeth, and the Montagues and Capulets in another play. For 10 points, name this British author who wrote the play Romeo and Juliet.

In one fresco by this man, St. Thomas raises his index figure in doubt as the central figure stretches his hands over a table. Another work by this artist shows a man with four arms inscribed in geometric shapes. This man depicted the wife of Francesco del Giocondo smiling mysteriously in another painting. For 10 points, name this Renaissance artist of Vitruvian Man and the Mona Lisa.

The Phoenix Mars Lander observed this type of cloud, which absorb outgoing infrared radiation but fail to deflect incoming sunlight, leading to a net heating effect. They can originate from the glaciation of other clouds, and jet contrails are a man-made form of these clouds. They are generally found in the upper atmosphere and are often associated with fair weather. For 10 points, identify this wispy type of cloud made of ice crystals.

In one scene of this work, a gravedigger unearths the skull of Yorick. Rosencrantz and Guildenstern were sent along with the titular character to England, who met Prince Fortinbras as his army marches toward Poland. Ophelia drowns to death and Laertes, urged on by Claudius, swears to avenge her death in a fencing match, only to see the plan fall apart as Gertrude mistakenly drinks the poisoned wine and everyone dies in the end. For 10 points, identify this Shakespearean play in which the titular character gives the "To Be, or Not To Be" monologue.

Early in his career, this author reworked Alice in Wonderland into political satires for the Westminster Gazette. A Sandie Byrne book about this "Unbearable" author coined the "feral ephebe" trope to characterize his early protagonists Reginald and Clovis. He parodied George Bernard Shaw's play Man and Superman with his collection Beasts and Super-Beasts, which contains a story in which a girl describes her family drowning in a bog while out hunting. This author, who created the polecat-ferret-worshipper Conradin, took his pen name from the Rubaiyat's word for "cupbearer." A story by him ends with the line "Romance at short notice was her specialty" after Framton Nuttel dashes from the Sappleton estate. For 10 points, name this British humorist of "Sredni Vashtar" and "The Open Window."

This character has sex with a woman who uses the names Corinna, Gertrude, and Ingrid in one novel after visiting Ataguitania. The founder of the Organization of Apocryphal Power is pursued by this character in a novel in which they read Tazio Bazakbal's novel outside the town of Malbork and meet with an expert on Cimmerian literature named Professor Uzzi-Tuzzi. This character is advised to "Relax. Concentrate. Dispel every other thought" in a novel where they fall in love with a girl named Ludmilla. For 10 points, name this protagonist of Italo Calvino's If on a winter's night a traveler, which is written in second person.
acceptableAnswers: accept the protagonist of If on a winter's night a traveler before mention

tossups.text: While quaestor, this man passed a bill which reduced patrician influence on elections by thinning the ramps to the voting platforms. This man nearly met his downfall over the formation of veteran's colonies on land north of the Po already owned by Roman citizens. The actions of Bocchus I led this man's greatest rival to capture a Numidian who this man defeated, Jugurtha. At the Battles of Vercellae and Aquae Sextiae, this man defeated invading Cimbri and Teutones tribes, actions for which he was called "the third founder of Rome." For 10 points, name this seven-time Roman consul and rival of Sulla known for his military reforms.

This property partly names a system created by University of Alberta student Sean Graham, intended to replace the SMP system. Satellite parties are used in Scorporo systems to reduce this property. In election results, a low value for the Gallagher index indicates a higher amount of this property. Parties winning many electoral districts can cause them to win overhang seats that reduce this property of election results. Germany originated a "mixed-member" system with this property, which is contrasted with parallel systems or mixed-member majoritarian systems. For 10 points, voting systems where political parties receive seats roughly equal to their percentage of the popular vote are named for what property and "representation"?
acceptableAnswers: mixed-member with “what other property names the system?”
MMP with “what does that stand for?”

tossups.text: Inventory control is modeled by the Markovian type of this concept, and in the Keynesian Cross, this equals the total output of an economy at efficiency. The Slutsky equation relates two forms of this. The Hicksian form of it assumes constant utility and is usually contrasted with the Marshallian form. Say's Law states that this is created by the presence of goods, and Keynes did work on the "aggregate" form of it. This quantity has a downward sloping curve and can be defined as the amount of a good or service consumers are willing to buy at a given price. For 10 points, identify this economic concept, commonly contrasted with supply.

Within a year of this empire's creation, Karl Mack von Leiberich and over twenty-five-thousand of its troops were captured at the Battle of Ulm. This empire was formed in 1804 by Francis II, who unified Habsburg-controlled lands, and in 1867, it became part of a "Dual Monarchy" with its neighbor. The dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire led to the creation of, for ten points, what European empire that was once united with its neighbor, Hungary?

During this dynasty, the Zhengtong emperor was captured during a campaign against the Oirat Mongols in the Tumu crisis. After winning the battle of Lake Poyang, the Hongwu emperor founded this dynasty. The Great Bao'en Temple was repaired by this dynasty's Xuande Emperor, who was the successor of the Yongle ["Yong-le"]Emperor. This dynasty was formed following the Red Turban Rebellion, and treasure voyages from this dynasty were led by Zheng He. For 10 points, name this dynasty that succeeded the Yuan and preceded the Qing, known for its porcelain vases.

A group of genes coding for lactose breakdown, known as the lac operon, was first discovered in this model organism. Although it is not Shigella, shiga toxins are produced in virulent strains of this organism such as its serotype O157:H7. They colonize the human gut at birth. For 10 points, name these gram-negative bacteria that are a common cause of food poisoning and food recalls.

The Pagina/12 newspaper falsely claimed that this man gave bread to Jorge Videla. This man said that, "The Earth is beginning to look like an immense pile of filth" in his Laudato Si . This man ordered the opening of doors as part of a Jubilee Year of Mercy decree. In February 2016, he suggested that contraceptives could be used in areas with Zika. He headlined the 2015 World Meeting of Families in Philadelphia and was formerly known as Jorge Bergoglio. For 10 points name this former Cardinal of Buenos Aires, the current pope.

This god was tricked into giving his true name in order to heal a snakebite. The goddess Sekhmet was often referred to as the "Eye" of this god, and nearly destroyed humanity before being fed red wine by him. This god, the grandfather of Nut (NOOT) and Geb, was primarily worshipped at Heliopolis. This god travels in the solar barge and fights against Apophis every night. For 10 points, identify this Egyptian god of the Sun.

parts.text: Name these beings from Yoruban (YOH-roo-bin) religions such as Santería. Examples include Ogun and Elegua.
Santería is this type of religion, meaning that it combines multiple religious traditions from belief systems such as Catholicism and Yoruba mythology.

To become a priest within Santería, people go through a ritual where they acquire "elekes," which are these objects. After receiving these objects, initiates bow over a bathtub to have their heads washed.

bonuses.leadin: One of these beings is frequently combined with Saint Peter within Santería. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This book, which is read on the holiday of Purim, detailing how Mordecai and Esther prevent a plot by Haman to kill the Jews of Persia.
This narrator of the Book of Ecclesiastes says things like "vanity of vanities; all is vanity" and "to everything there is a season, and a time to every purpose under heaven."
In this erotic book of the Bible, the male voice proclaims "my sister, my bride, how much better is thy love than wine!" while the female exclaims "thy neck is like the tower of David."

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer the following about the Five Scrolls in the Tanakh.

parts.text: Name these objects, nine of which are placed in the menorah for Hanukkah, with one being lit each day.

Women light candles every week to mark this Jewish religious observance, during which people traditionally abstain from work and attend synagogue services. It usually occurs from Friday evening to Saturday evening.
The Hanukkah candles represent the lamp oil which miraculously lasted for eight days during a revolt led by this group of Jewish warriors.

bonuses.leadin: After lighting these objects, women cover their hands and recite a blessing. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with t cells and cell-mediated immunity.
What is the main function of the T cell in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to t cells and cell-mediated immunity.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Name this Austrian father of psychoanalysis.
Freud discusses the "oceanic feeling" in this 1929 work that examines the tensions between the individual and modern society.
Freud called these entities the "royal road to the unconscious" and described their purpose as "wish fulfillment" in a work titled for their "Interpretation".

bonuses.leadin: This man theorized about the libido and transference and the unconscious and repression and a bunch of other really important crap. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this religion that began when Siddhartha Gautama (sid-HART-ah gow-TAH-mah) achieved nirvana.
Buddhists adhere to this set of four teachings, which include ones on suffering and on path that leads to the end of suffering.
This branch and Mahayana are the two main branches of Buddhism. It is referred to as "the Lesser Vehicle" and is predominantly practiced in Sri Lanka (SHREE LONK - ah).

bonuses.leadin: Variants of one branch of this religion include Pure Land and Zen. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this short story in which the married couple Della and Jim Young give up their most prized possessions in an attempt to provide each other the perfect gift for Christmas.
This author, whose short story "The Last Leaf" depicts Johnsy surviving pneumonia because of a leaf painted on an ivy plant, also wrote "The Gift of the Magi."
O. Henry also wrote about Bill and Sam Driskoll, two crooks who abduct Ebenezer Dorset's red-haired son. Because the kid is so obnoxious, they pay Ebenezer $250 so they can return him.

bonuses.leadin: Prior to selling her hair to Madame Sofronie for twenty dollars, one character in this work saved up one dollar and eighty-seven cents for a christmas present. For ten points each:

parts.text: Identify this American composer who wrote the overture to The School for Scandal and Symphony in One Movement.
Samuel Barber may be best known for this work, the second movement of his String Quartet, Opus 11.
This other American composer wrote Fanfare for the Common Man, Billy the Kid, and a song called "Simple Gifts" in his Appalachian Spring.

bonuses.leadin: He was twice awarded the Pulitzer Prize for his opera Vanessa and his Concerto for Piano and Orchestra. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this model organism often used in genetic studies due to its simplicity and short lifespan.
Morgan's work with fruit flies built on the studies of this "Father of Genetics". This Austrian monk's work with pea plants led him to formulate his laws of segregation and independent assortment.

These genes, first discovered in fruit flies in 1894, regulate the body layout and development of most organisms. Examples include the Ultrabithorax gene, which controls leg and haltere wing formation along the thorax.

bonuses.leadin: Thomas Hunt Morgan studied the inheritance of white and red eyes in these organisms, from which he developed the theory of sex-linked characteristics. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this animal that also possesses some "fearful symmetry."
Identify the poet of The Tyger, which is included in his collection Songs of Experience, not his Songs of Innocence.
Blake is said to be one of the first members of this artistic movement, which focused on a return to raw emotion and nature and reaction against rationalization and aristocracy.

bonuses.leadin: This animal is said to be "burning bright / In the forests of the night." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this poet. Many of his Pythian Odes, like the one calling Hippocleas one of "Sparta's warlike sons," are dedicated to winners of athletic competitions.
This Cavalier poet called his love a "slug-a-bed" in "Corinna's going a-Maying." He tells some young women to "gather ye rosebuds while ye may" in the most famous poem from his Hesperides.
The death of the "prince of mimics" inspired this Roman to write a poem "On the Death of Corinna's Parrot." His Metamorphoses serves as a collection of mythical transformations.

bonuses.leadin: This writer called Corinna of Tanagra a pig after she beat him in a poetry contest. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this language used to describe a "frail vessel [which] thou emptiest again and again." That poem written in this language opens: "Thou hast made me endless, such is thy pleasure."

This Bengali poet translated selections from his Gitanjali into English, and included them in the collection Song Offerings. As a playwright, his literary output includes Red Oleanders and The Post Office.
The preface to Tagore's Song Offerings was written by this other writer, whose own poems include "The Lake Isle of Innisfree" and "The Wild Swans at Coole."

bonuses.leadin: A poem written in this language is set in a place "where the mind is without fear" and "where knowledge is free." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this university whose alumni included Jean Calvin, Denis Diderot, Voltaire and Honoré de Balzac. It was located in the Sorbonne district of its namesake city.
In its early days, the University of Paris had four faculties: in Arts, Law, Medicine and this other discipline. Professors in this most prestigious faculty included Thomas Aquinas.
The University of Paris was dissolved after a series of student protests which began in May of this year. Fearing revolution, Charles de Gaulle fled to Germany, but was persuaded to return.

bonuses.leadin: This university was the second oldest in Europe, founded after Bologna but predating both Oxford and Cambridge. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these disorders, examples of which include bulimia and anorexia.
acceptableAnswers: accept anything that describes problems with eating

parts.text: The Minnesota Starvation Experiment was performed during World War II and used these people as test subjects, many of whom were members of Historic Peace Churches such as the Quakers.
acceptableAnswers: anything suggesting a refusal to perform military service

parts.text: The experiment provided valuable data on this condition, which can occur when a malnourished person consumes too much food over a short period of time. Clinical indicators for this condition include phosphate and potassium deficiency.

bonuses.leadin: The results of the Minnesota Starvation Experiment have greatly influenced the treatment of these conditions. For ten points each:

parts.text: In this Richard Adams novel, a group of rabbits leave their warren and search for a new one. On the way, they encounter socialist and totalitarian rabbit communities before creating a democracy.
In this George Orwell novel that parodies the Russian Revolution, a group of pigs lead a barnyard revolt.
In Animal Farm, this bird represents the church. The pigs initially distrust this character's tales of Sugarcandy Mountain, but as conditions on the farm worsen, they welcome him back.

bonuses.leadin: Some books use animal societies to model human ones. Answer some questions about surprisingly political animals, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this African dictator who expelled colonial influences from his country, in addition to renaming it Zaire.
This current nation with capital at Kinshasa, which is currently torn apart by war and a rape epidemic in its Katanga province, was known as Zaire during Mobutu's reign.
The Democratic Republic of the Congo was once a colony of this European country, whose capital is Brussels. This country's King Leopold II personally profited from the exploitation of the DRC.

bonuses.leadin: This ruler took over in 1965 after arresting Patrice Lumumba. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this Chinese dynasty, renowned for its blue and white porcelain, which succeeded the Yuan dynasty and preceded the Qing dynasty.
The aforementioned explorer, Zheng He, brought exotic animals to China from the East African coast with this name. The Bantu language of this name is the most widely spoken in Africa.
Zheng He made his massive voyages using junks, a type of this vessel. Lateen sails helped merchants and sailors cross the Indian Ocean in these vessels during monsoon season.

bonuses.leadin: In his pseudo-historical book 1421, Gavin Menzies claimed that an explorer from this dynasty visited the Americas before Christopher Columbus. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this process that results in the formation of gametes. This process results in a haploid cell, unlike a similarly named process in somatic cells that creates new diploid cells.
The anaphase stage of both mitosis and meiosis pulls apart these X shaped structures in the cells that contain genes, normally found in the nucleus.

One aspect of meiosis is the "crossing over" of genes, which adds genetic variability. This phenomenon is when a pair of genes are close together and are usually inherited together, explaining why people with freckles often have red hair.

bonuses.leadin: The synaptonemal complex forms in one stage of this process. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Constitutional amendment that guarantees freedom of religion, as well as four other fundamental freedoms.

This founding father wrote the letter to the Danbury Baptists. This man cut and pasted select sections of the New Testament, omitting the miracles, into a work he called The Life and Morals of Jesus of Nazareth.

The Danbury Baptists wrote to Jefferson out of concern that this state, their home, maintained a different official state religion and may rescind rights of the minority. In 1818, this state disestablished its state church and ratified a new Constitution at a convention in Hartford.

bonuses.leadin: One section of this amendment is praised in an 1802 reply to the Danbury Baptists for "building a wall of separation between Church and State." For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this animal-human hybrid from Greek mythology, for which Daedalus [DED-ah-lus] built a maze-like labyrinth.
This Athenian hero ventured into the Labyrinth to slay the Minotaur. This hero's father committed suicide when this hero forgot to switch his sails from black to white upon returning to Athens.
This princess gave Theseus a ball of string to keep him from getting lost in the Labyrinth. According to some sources, she became the consort of Dionysus after being abandoned by Theseus.

bonuses.leadin: Seven boys and seven girls were regularly sent to be used as sacrifices to this creature. For 10 points each,
